text:
You want a Next JS blog setup with an EditorJS-based post workflow that can generate structured outlines and titles from a short user prompt, then let the user review and expand each section in the editor.

I’m Noor Halden, and I’d be glad to build this workflow for you. I have 6 years of experience working with Python and machine learning tools, including OpenAI API, LangChain, Hugging Face Transformers, PyTorch, scikit-learn, NLP, XGBoost, and pandas. For this project, I’d focus on creating a clean, reliable GPT-backed content flow that fits naturally into your existing blog template and keeps the implementation practical for Next JS.

I’ve recently built a call centre speech analytics pipeline for Vantor Call Centers using Python, Whisper, pyannote, OpenAI API, and PostgreSQL. That system transcribed calls, separated agent and customer speech, and wrote a QA summary for every call. One result was increasing QA coverage from 3% to 100% of calls.

For your blog generator, I would start by adapting the template to support EditorJS, leaving out the pieces you said you don’t need such as Giscus, analytics, newsletter, and the other optional services. I’d make sure the deployment path is suitable for Vercel and keep the structure aligned with the starter setup you referenced. Then I’d build the post creator flow so the editor first asks the user for a 2–3 sentence description of the article. That input would be sent with fetch to an API route in the same project, which would call the OpenAI GPT API with your prompt and return the result in EditorJS-friendly JSON.

From there, I’d render the outline in EditorJS and add a custom plugin/button for each heading so the user can generate body content section by section. The goal would be a smooth drafting experience where the outline is created automatically, but the user still has control over editing and refinement inside the editor.

If you’d like, I can help turn this into a maintainable workflow that is straightforward to extend later.
